ov: About 95 species of brightly coloured reef fish whose teeth are fused into a parrot-like beak, most diverse in the Indo-Pacific. They scrape algae from coral and rock, grind it up and excrete the rest as sand. Most start life as females and later change into males.

why.et: Larger species are fished commercially, mainly in the Indo-Pacific, but most species are not heavily fished.

len: Mostly 30–50 cm; green humphead up to 1.3 m
rg: Coral reefs, rocky coasts and seagrass beds; most species live in the Indo-Pacific.
df: Algae scraped from coral and rock, dead coral and rubble, seagrass, and sometimes live coral.
fx: Some wrap themselves in a mucus cocoon at night, probably to hide their scent from predators.
Early scientists named more than 350 species, almost four times the real number, because the colour phases look so different.
